sentences.l2: 很久以前，人们想写音乐。
sentences.l1: A long time ago, people wanted to write music.

sentences.l2: 他们不知道怎么写。
sentences.l1: They did not know how to write it.

sentences.l2: 后来，有人开始画符号。
sentences.l1: Later, someone began to draw symbols.

sentences.l2: 这些符号告诉人们哪个音要唱。
sentences.l1: These symbols told people which note to sing.

sentences.l2: 这是最早的记谱法。
sentences.l1: This was the earliest music notation.

sentences.l2: 记谱法就是写音乐的方法。
sentences.l1: Music notation is a way of writing music.

sentences.l2: 不同的地方有不同的记谱法。
sentences.l1: Different places have different music notations.

sentences.l2: 有些人用字母，有些人用数字。
sentences.l1: Some people use letters, and some people use numbers.

sentences.l2: 音乐理论也慢慢变多了。
sentences.l1: Music theory also slowly grew.

sentences.l2: 作曲家喜欢写音乐。
sentences.l1: Composers like to write music.

sentences.l2: 他们需要记谱法帮忙。
sentences.l1: They need music notation to help.

sentences.l2: 没有记谱法，音乐很容易忘记。
sentences.l1: Without music notation, music is easily forgotten.

sentences.l2: 几百年前，欧洲的作曲家用了新的记谱法。
sentences.l1: Several hundred years ago, European composers used a new music notation.

sentences.l2: 这个方法用五条线。
sentences.l1: This method uses five lines.

sentences.l2: 音符在不同的位置，声音就不一样。
sentences.l1: When notes are in different positions, the sounds are different.

sentences.l2: 这个方法很好用。
sentences.l1: This method is very easy to use.

sentences.l2: 很多人开始学。
sentences.l1: Many people began to learn it.

sentences.l2: 慢慢地，这种记谱法传到了别的国家。
sentences.l1: Slowly, this music notation spread to other countries.

sentences.l2: 记谱法一直在发展。
sentences.l1: Music notation has kept developing.

sentences.l2: 今天的记谱法比以前清楚多了。
sentences.l1: Today's music notation is much clearer than before.

sentences.l2: 学习音乐的人觉得方便。
sentences.l1: People who learn music find it convenient.

sentences.l2: 历史告诉我们，好的方法是慢慢来的。
sentences.l1: History tells us that good methods come slowly.
